note: The Part 8 hard floor. Set from the first repeated sweep: 5 gold questions x 2 prompt versions x 3 repetitions, 30 runs, 2026-08-10. Every number below sits in a gap where no observed case straddles it — the Part 6 threshold rule, confirmed by repetition rather than assumed.
why_content_and_not_grounded: Measured, not argued. Across ten cells of three repetitions each, CONTENT pass was stable in 10 of 10 — every cell landed 0/3 or 3/3, with nothing in between. GROUNDED was unstable in 3 of 10: the same question, the same evidence, the same prompt, at temperature 0, produced different grounding verdicts. A floor on `grounded` would be measuring the sampler. A floor on content is measuring the pipeline.
calibrated_from: SUPERSEDED — see calibrated_from_sweeps, which names the four Block E archives this floor now stands on. CORRECTED 2026-08-28: this key previously read 'eval/sweeps/20260810T191414-p7-answer-v2r_p7-answer-v4-r3.json', the sweep whose calibration was invalidated hours after being set (see calibration_invalidated). calibrate_floor --write left it untouched on 2026-08-28, so a stale provenance pointer stood beside calibrated: true and read as current. calibrate_floor now maintains this key, so the defect cannot recur.
required_cases_note: Each must pass in EVERY repetition, not on average. Expressed per case rather than as an aggregate rate because an aggregate lets a total failure on one question be paid for by successes on others, and the questions are not interchangeable. Removing a case because the model had a bad session is how a floor is quietly lowered to whatever is currently passing, and that sentence stands. SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-08-26: this note previously read 'vimose-runes is retained as required DESPITE failing the second sweep, because the failure is not a regression in the pipeline - the evidence block is bit-identical and the corpus edit never touched it.' That was written when the failure looked like one bad session. It is now 0/3 on two distinct dates and the dry run locates it in retrieval. See demotions.vimose-runes, which records the evidence and the condition that puts it back.

known_failing_cases.aksum-exports: Fails 0/3 under BOTH prompt versions, and 4/4 across the archived Part 7 runs — seven consecutive failures under four prompts. The corpus contains the answer in published English, aligned by section, verified present in the evidence block by the sweep's dry run. This is not a prompt defect and must not be folded into the floor as tolerated; it is an open defect tracked separately so that a floor pass can never be read as 'the system answers these questions'. CROSS-ARM, 2026-08-28, and it does not rescue this case. On chat-strong at temperature 1 (eval/arms/20260828T155443-p7-answer-v2r-r5-chat-strong-t1.json) it passes 1/5 and REFUSES 3/5, naming what it cannot find: 'no source names Aksum; the closest material concerns trade goods exchanged at Adulis'. The attribution to prompt and retrieval survives a second model. The Adulis discriminator held on that arm too - adulis-exports 5/5 against this case's 1/5 - which is the discriminator doing its job on evidence it had never seen. Ruling 36: that archive is read BESIDE this floor and never inside it, and it moves nothing here.
known_failing_cases.vimose-runes: Demoted from required_cases on 2026-08-26, on evidence from two dates. 0/3 in the 2026-08-24 session and 0/3 in the 2026-08-25 session, corpus digest 26e4a683... asserted at both ends of both sweeps, and FINDING 18 records it as deterministic on BOTH days about a different answer - so this is not a flaky sampler. The D4 dry run locates the failure in retrieval, not generation: its own gold record scandinavia-03-vimose sits at rank 3, sim 0.384, behind arabia-04-jabal-dabub at 0.433 and arabia-03-jsnab17 at 0.401, a spread of 0.049, and no other case in the pilot has a margin like it. Tracked here rather than deleted, on the aksum-exports precedent, so that a floor pass can never be read as 'the system answers this question'. A sweep that reports it passing is a finding, not a success. What would put it back is written in demotions.vimose-runes. CROSS-ARM, 2026-08-28, and this one IS model-limited. On chat-strong at temperature 1 (eval/arms/20260828T155443-p7-answer-v2r-r5-chat-strong-t1.json) it passes 5/5 with a real hedged gloss - 'likely a personal name', 'possibly Mari (the famous one) is the sword of Alla' - where haiku refused 12/12. The case definition is unchanged since D3, so the move is the arm and nothing else. TWO rules keep this outside the floor and they are both deliberate: ruling 36 (an arm is read beside this floor, never inside it) and ruling 37 (reinstatement is measured at the corpus in force and on the DECLARED arm). This is NOT a step toward reinstatement and must never be read as one.
known_failing_cases.skz-titulature: RULING 42, 2026-08-28. Fails 0/12 across four sessions and three dates — 2026-08-26 (x2), 2026-08-27, 2026-08-28 — on ONE assertion, expect_answer_contains_any ['Ardashir', 'Ardašīr'], while satisfying every other assertion the case makes and resolving four quotations. This is tracked as an open defect and not corrected away, because the evidence was in front of it: persia-01-skz's §1 is a single titulature formula — 'I, the Mazda-worshipping god Shapur, king of kings of Iran and Not-Iran, whose race is of the gods, son of the Mazda-worshipping god Ardashir, king of kings of Iran, whose race is of the gods, grandson of the god King Pabag, am lord of Iran' — and the answer quoted from that sentence and stopped at Shapur's own epithets, dropping both genealogical clauses. WHAT WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: dropping the Ardashir group, which is the floor lowered to what is currently passing on the strength of a case that has never passed; and amending the question to ask for the filiation, which would orphan the twelve archived runs because match_case joins on question text. The weaker half of this is the QUESTION — 'what titles does Shapur I claim' does not plainly ask for the filiation — and that is a note for how the 36 new records are written, not a licence to rewrite this one. CROSS-ARM, 2026-08-28, and this one IS model-limited. On chat-strong at temperature 1 (eval/arms/20260828T155443-p7-answer-v2r-r5-chat-strong-t1.json) it passes 5/5 on the case EXACTLY as ruling 42 refused to amend it: the Ardashir group is still asserted and is now satisfied. That is what the arm was run to find out, and it is not a reason to change the case - the weaker half of ruling 42 stands, that a question which does not plainly ask for the filiation is a note for how the 36 new records are written. Ruling 36: read beside this floor, never inside it.

max_refusal_rate_note: Observed 0.40 for p7-answer-v2r and 0.60 for p7-answer-v4. 0.5 sits in the gap with no observation on it. Refusal rate is a floor term in its own right because citation hygiene is maximised by saying as little as possible: a prompt that refuses more while erring no less is a regression, and no metric built on grounding can see it.
max_unstable_content_cells_note: Observed 0 for both prompt versions. If a content cell ever splits across its own repetitions, the floor stops being measurable before it stops being met, and that must fail loudly rather than average out.
min_distinct_dates_note: D4, 2026-08-24. eval/calibrate_floor.py REFUSES to write calibrated: true from sweeps spanning fewer than this many distinct session dates, and the refusal is mutation-verified. Three, because calibration_invalidated below records a floor set from one day's observation and contradicted the same day. Dates rather than sessions is TASK 3 as specified on 2026-08-20; sessions are the finer observation and are counted and reported beside the dates, because the pair of sweeps that invalidated this floor were two sessions on ONE date. Three sessions in one afternoon are three sessions and one date, and they calibrate nothing. A sweep carrying no session identity contributes no date and cannot be given one after the fact.
min_repetitions_note: A single shot is one sample of a distribution nobody has looked at. Part 6 measured a 0.317 chrF spread within one case at temperature 0; this sweep found three grounding verdicts flipping on identical input. Checking the floor against an unrepeated run is not checking it. Superseded in part: three repetitions in a single session proved insufficient to detect a case that swings completely between sessions. Repetitions should span sessions before any threshold here is called calibrated again.
cross_check: The floor is a REGRESSION gate, not a definition of success. It says the four questions that work still work, and that the system has not bought tidiness with silence. It says nothing about whether the corpus is large enough or the answers good enough — those are Part 10 questions.
calibration_invalidated: 2026-08-10, hours after being set. The floor was calibrated on the observation that CONTENT was stable in 10 of 10 cells across three repetitions each. A second sweep, with the vimose-runes evidence block BYTE-IDENTICAL (sha256 verified across all six archived runs), produced the opposite result: 3/3 pass with seven resolved quotations in the first session, 0/3 with none in the second. Same prompt version, same model, same evidence, temperature 0. The stability that justified this floor was itself a single sample.
session_caveat: REPETITIONS WITHIN ONE SESSION ARE CORRELATED AND ARE NOT INDEPENDENT SAMPLES. Both sweeps were internally consistent — 3/3 one way, then 3/3 the other — so repetition inside a session measures a mode, not a distribution. Part 6's lesson was 'one shot is one sample of a distribution nobody has looked at'. This is the same lesson one level up: three shots in one session may also be one sample. Until repetitions span sessions, this floor is a WITHIN-SESSION regression gate and nothing more.

vimose-runes.evidence: 0/3 in SIX sessions over FIVE distinct UTC dates: 2026-08-24 (792202e7ac58), 2026-08-25 (8ee2273defd6), 2026-08-26 (37f79c93b79a and 0c74d52b2c25), 2026-08-27 (6715f2a3ab6b), 2026-08-28 (6a382f4f9ac7). One corpus digest 26e4a683... asserted at both ends of every sweep, temperature 0. Extended 2026-08-28 from the two dates the demotion was originally taken on.
vimose-runes.diagnosis: NOT DIAGNOSED, and the recorded diagnosis was wrong. CORRECTED 2026-08-28; the superseded text is kept in superseded_diagnosis. It read 'retrieval margin, not generation' on the ground that scandinavia-03-vimose ranks 3rd at sim 0.384 behind two unrelated Arabian inscriptions. FINDING 21 (2026-08-26) contradicts it over the full 33-case set: jabal-dabub-basmala has the WORST displacement in the entire set (rank 3, sim 0.388, spread 0.135 from [S1]) and passes 3/3; muziris-cargo, a REQUIRED case, sits at rank 2 inside vimose's own margin and passes 3/3. Rank and margin predict nothing about the verdict. What is left is a negative result: the cause recorded here was ruled out and no replacement is supported by the evidence. Writing a second mechanism down now, on no more evidence than the first one had, is the error this field exists to prevent. What IS measured: 0/3 and grounded 0/3 in all six sessions, with the answer text moving underneath a fixed verdict — 3 distinct texts, then 2, 2, 2, and 1 on 2026-08-28.
vimose-runes.reinstated_when: The case passes 3/3 in each of THREE sessions on THREE distinct UTC dates, at the corpus in force when the reinstatement is claimed. RAISED 2026-08-28, Block F decision 4, from two sessions on two dates. FINDING 26 is the whole reason: 2026-08-28 produced a case unanimous across THREE sessions that flipped on the fourth, so two dates of agreement is a bar this project has direct evidence is too low. Three is not a new number — it is min_distinct_dates, which this file already imposes on its own calibration, and reusing it is deliberate: a bar invented for one case is a bar chosen for that case. Applied identically to promotion_candidates.weilue-chinese-quotation, in the same decision, so that the standard for coming back is the standard for going up. PREVIOUSLY, and superseded: 'The case passes 3/3 in each of two sessions on two distinct UTC dates. CORRECTED 2026-08-28: this condition was previously keyed to scandinavia-03-vimose being retrieved at [S1] under a dry run, which FINDING 21 shows is neither necessary (cases pass from rank 3 with worse margins) nor sufficient (rank predicts no verdict in this set), and to “not before Block F, because retrieval is frozen”, which presumed a retrieval fix the evidence does not support.' No mechanism is named here, on purpose, and raising the bar does not name one either.
vimose-runes.why_this_is_not_a_licence: A demotion is admissible in this file only with evidence from more than one date, a diagnosis, and a written condition for return. Without all three it is a floor lowered to whatever is currently passing. eval/goldset.py refuses a demotion that omits any of them.
vimose-runes.superseded_diagnosis: Retrieval margin, not generation. scandinavia-03-vimose ranks 3rd at sim 0.384 behind two unrelated Arabian inscriptions at 0.433 and 0.401. Block E cannot address this: retrieval and the corpus are frozen for the whole block.
vimose-runes.corrected_on: 2026-08-28, Block E close. The DEMOTION stands on the evidence above; the reasoning recorded beside it did not survive the block.

calibration_scope.rule: A sweep contributes to calibration only if it carries a session identity AND ran at least min_cases_per_sweep cases. A sweep that fails the rule blocks calibration outright UNLESS it is named in excluded_by_rule, with the reason it fails written beside it.
calibration_scope.declared_on: 2026-08-26, before Block E day 1, for the reason the whole block is decided in advance: the rule between days is change nothing, and a scope settled on day 3 is a scope chosen after seeing the numbers.
calibration_scope.why: Two separate problems, one rule. (a) Three sweeps archived before D4 carry no session identity and can never be given one, so while calibrate_floor refuses on ANY undated sweep, calibrated: true is unreachable at any number of dates - not merely blocked until three. That was not visible in the D4 report, which refused on the date count first. (b) The two D4 pilot sweeps ran six cases where Block E runs the full stratified set, and a floor calibrated across a 6-case date and a 30-case date is a floor whose denominator changes between dates. Excluding them by a recorded rule is a diff. Excluding them by moving files is not, and is forbidden.
calibration_scope.what_exclusion_does_not_mean: The two pilot sweeps are excluded from CALIBRATION only. They carry real session identity, they count toward both stability numbers, and they are the archives the variance decomposition was built and mutation-verified against.

calibration_scope.a_named_sweep_must_actually_fail_the_rul: eval/answer_eval.py REFUSES an exclusion naming a sweep that satisfies the rule. Without that, this list is a place to put a sweep whose numbers are inconvenient, which is the move calibrate_floor exists to make impossible.

arm.declared_on: 2026-08-28, Block F decision 2 — BEFORE the sonnet arm ran, and for that reason. A scope settled after seeing an arm's numbers is a scope chosen to fit them, which is the same argument calibration_scope.why already makes about the case-count clause.
arm.rule: A sweep calibrates only if its arm is BOTH identifiable AND equal to the pair above. A sweep on any other arm fails the rule and therefore blocks calibration unless it is named in excluded_by_rule — where naming it is legitimate, because it genuinely fails.
arm.why_the_arm_had_to_become_part_of_the_ru: Without this clause the anti-loophole becomes the loophole. A sonnet arm at temperature 1 carries a session identity, runs the full 33 cases and archives complete, so it satisfies every other clause; a_named_sweep_must_actually_fail_the_rule would then REFUSE to let it be excluded by name, and this file would insist that a temperature-1 sonnet sweep calibrate a floor set on greedy haiku. Found on 2026-08-28 while planning the arm, not after running it.
arm.how_the_nine_legacy_sweeps_are_read: None of the nine archives records an arm: every Block E number is denominated in a model and a temperature that were facts about the code on the day rather than about the file — FINDING 14's defect one layer up. eval.answer_eval.sweep_arm reconstructs the arm for them from what IS on disk and says so. The ALIAS is read from serving_stack.model on the rows: Block E correction 4 established that field is the echo of the string SENT and cannot move, which is what makes it useless as a drift detector and faithful as a record of what was asked for. The TEMPERATURE is not in the archive at all and is ASSUMED to be 0, because answer.assemble.assemble had no temperature parameter until 2026-08-28 and the answer path could not send another value. That is a claim about the code, it is labelled 'reconstructed' rather than 'recorded' in every report, and it is available to exactly the nine sweeps that predate the change. A sweep archived after it must state its arm or fail.
arm.what_this_does_not_do: It does not make the sonnet arm inadmissible evidence. It makes the sonnet arm inadmissible as a CALIBRATION INPUT to a floor set on a different model. The arm archives to eval/arms/, reports its own numbers, and is read beside this floor and never inside it.

corpus.declared_on: 2026-08-31, F3, BEFORE record 25 was ingested and for that reason. Ruling 49. This is the last moment the clause can be written by someone who has not seen what the first sub-tranche did to the numbers - ruling 39's argument, for the fifth time in this block and the last block in which it can be made in advance.
corpus.rule: A sweep calibrates only if its corpus is BOTH identifiable AND equal to the pair above. A sweep at any other corpus fails the rule and therefore blocks calibration unless it is named in excluded_by_rule - where naming it is legitimate, because it genuinely fails. A sweep whose corpus MOVED under it (corpus_version != corpus_version_after) fails for a second reason and cannot be rescued by matching either end.
corpus.why_the_corpus_had_to_become_part_of_the: Ruling 36's own sentence, one dimension over. Without this clause, the moment record 25 is ingested a sweep at 33 records carries a session identity, runs the full 33 cases, states its arm and archives complete - so it satisfies every other clause - and a_named_sweep_must_actually_fail_the_rule then REFUSES to let it be excluded by name. This file would INSIST that a 33-record sweep calibrate a floor set at 24. The data was already there and the rule did not read it: FINDING 14 put corpus_version into every archive precisely so that a corpus which moved could not go unnoticed, calibration_scope was then written twice - on 2026-08-26 and again by ruling 36 - without ever reaching for it, and eval/calibrate_floor.py contained zero occurrences of the string 'corpus'. Two entries in this file already anticipated the clause: promotion_candidates.weilue-chinese-quotation.bar and demotions.vimose-runes.reinstated_when both name the corpus as part of a claim's identity.
corpus.what_this_does_NOT_do: It does not suspend the floor. The floor stays IN FORCE as a regression gate across the whole corpus move: a run at 33 records still computes a verdict on required_cases, and a required case that stops passing is exactly the regression this floor exists to catch. What the clause removes is that run's ability to RE-CALIBRATE - to write calibrated: true, and with it a new calibrated_stability - from a corpus the floor was never set on. In force, and not self-renewing, are two different properties and this file now holds both.
corpus.how_a_mid_tranche_reading_is_taken: eval/run_answer_sweep.py archives a run below min_cases_per_sweep to eval/probes/ and never to eval/sweeps/, exactly as a foreign arm archives to eval/arms/. eval/calibrate_floor.load_sweeps globs sweeps/*.json only, so a probe cannot calibrate BY CONSTRUCTION and excluded_by_rule does not grow one entry per sub-tranche. Ruling 51 makes the probe the floor's mid-tranche reading: the three required cases at min_repetitions, ~9 chat calls against a full sweep's ~198. A rule enforced by the directory is a rule nobody has to remember, and the scope clause above is still the guard if a file is ever moved across by hand.
corpus.recalibration_at_60: This clause is re-declared to the 60-record count and digest, and calibration re-runs only from sweeps at that corpus. min_distinct_dates is 3, so re-calibration costs THREE sessions at 60 on three distinct UTC dates. G3's amendment booked two. Ruling 50 books the third as a ninth session in Block F, which is also the date promotion_and_reinstatement_bar already required - at 60 - of weilue-chinese-quotation and vimose-runes, and which nothing had booked either. Three rules in this repository needed a third date at 60 and the gate booked two: found 2026-08-31 in F3, before record 25, rather than on the last afternoon of the block.

weilue-chinese-quotation.why_it_moved: The entry said the case FAILS and recorded, in its own corrected text, that it passes 12/12. A file that states a falsified claim about a case is worse through a corpus move than either resolution of it, and Block E kept it only because of the freeze, which lifted at 1bdaf04. It is not failing, so it does not belong in known_failing_cases; it has not met the bar, so it does not belong in required_cases. This is the third state, and it exists because the file needed one.
weilue-chinese-quotation.evidence: 3/3 in each of four sessions across three distinct UTC dates — 2026-08-26 (37f79c93b79a, 0c74d52b2c25), 2026-08-27 (6715f2a3ab6b), 2026-08-28 (6a382f4f9ac7). Corpus digest 26e4a683... asserted at both ends of all four sweeps, temperature 0, chat-default. Chinese source text resolved in the answer. Its TEXT is not stable: 1 distinct text in each of the first three sessions and 2 on 2026-08-28, with the day-2 and day-3 answers sharing 0.16 of their characters — the verdict held and the text did not, which is FINDING 25 inside the one case that had been immune to it.
weilue-chinese-quotation.bar: 3/3 in each of THREE sessions on THREE distinct UTC dates, at 60 records. The same bar as demotions.vimose-runes.reinstated_when, deliberately: one standard, applied to a case coming up and a case going down, decided once on 2026-08-28 rather than twice on the days each case happened to be in front of someone.
weilue-chinese-quotation.why_the_existing_evidence_does_not_promo: It would, on any bar phrased in sessions and dates — 4 sessions and 3 dates already exceeds the bar above. What it does not satisfy is the CORPUS: all twelve runs are denominated in 26e4a683, 24 records, and Block F moves the corpus to 60. Promoting a case into required_cases on evidence from a corpus that is about to be replaced is how a regression gate comes to be guaranteed by an archive nobody can re-run. The bar is therefore not 'more sessions' but 'the same three-session standard, at the corpus the floor will be defending'.
weilue-chinese-quotation.never_subtracted_from_it: A candidate is not a pass and not a failure. It is reported beside the floor verdict, exactly as known_failing_cases is, and counts toward neither.

promotion_and_reinstatement_bar: ONE bar, decided 2026-08-28 as Block F decision 4 and applied in both directions: 3/3 in each of three sessions on three distinct UTC dates, at the corpus in force when the claim is made. A case may not be promoted into required_cases, nor reinstated to it, on anything less. Written here as well as in the two entries it governs, because a standard that exists only inside the record of the case it was applied to is a standard the next case gets to renegotiate.
